item.content:encoded:
Pennsylvania sports betting has boomed since its launch on Oct. 30, 2017. Since the Pennsylvania Gaming Control Board granted licenses to its first operators, options have expanded to 11 legal sportsbooks that you can enjoy. 

Yes, sports betting is legal in Pennsylvania. It has been legal since Oct. 30, 2017. You must have your account verified, be within the state of Pennsylvania, and be over the age of 21 to participate. 

Determining which sportsbook is best for you can be difficult. No matter if you are new or experienced with Pennsylvania Sportsbooks, we have compiled a list for you to evaluate options. Below is a list of the operators of Pennsylvania sportsbooks, including benefits, welcome offers, and any drawbacks to consider. 

Pennsylvania Sportsbooks offer Welcome Offers to new users in an effort to help them get acclimated to an app and sports betting in general. Welcome offers can change regularly, but the common types are bonus bets, first-bet-match, and deposit matches. Bonus bets are not the same as cash, but allow you to wager and collect the winnings. If you lose, it isn’t real money that you’ve lost. 

A first-bet-match offer is provided, so users can place wagers over a day or set period of time and receive the same amount (usually up to $100 per day) back. For example, if you place a $20 wager on day one, you’ll receive a $20 bonus in return. 

Deposit matches provide you with bonus value in the same amount as your initial deposit. Some Pennsylvania sportsbooks offer up to $1,000 in a deposit match. The match is playable but cannot be withdrawn. 

Sports betting became legal in Pennsylvania in October 2017 under Act 42 of 2017. Retail sportsbooks started launching in late 2018. Apps launched shortly thereafter in May 2019. Anyone over 21 and within the state lines can wager on professional and collegiate events. 

There is no shortage of top teams to bet on in Pennsylvania. Having two big cities in the state helps with the Philadelphia Eagles and Pittsburgh Steelers being prominent teams. Football always tends to be popular among bettors and the recent success of both teams has brought in extra interest. There are also two hockey teams and two baseball teams in the state. For baseball, they have the Phillies and the Pirates, both with plenty of stars. The Penguins and Flyers drive the NHL market in the state. If basketball is your sport, the 76ers can provide you with betting options from October until potentially June.

College sports betting in Pennsylvania is legal. However, you can only bet on sides, totals, and spreads. You can do some props like team totals, and parlays. There are a lot of options but one thing that is prohibited is betting on collegiate player props. You can bet on in-state teams and futures for teams like Penn State or Pittsburgh. This is not legal in every state, but is legal in Pennsylvania. 

There are 12 different retail sportsbooks in Pennsylvania. All of these retail sportsbook locations are found inside of casinos across the state. There are multiple options for placing a wager once you are there. Some provide self-service kiosks, while others also have people taking wagers from bettors.

item.description: Compare the best DFS apps and promos for 2026. See daily fantasy welcome bonuses, contest types and reviews to pick the right app.
item.content:encoded:
With the legalization of sports betting across multiple states over the past few years, daily fantasy hasn’t been at the forefront quite as much. However, it hasn’t gone away by any means, and there are still plenty of great options if you love daily fantasy. Daily fantasy sports apps are abundant, and their promotions are often enough to convince new users to give them a chance. Below, we’ll break down the best DFS apps and help you decide which DFS promos are right for you.

Every site is competing for you and your money, so naturally, they all offer incentives to use their DFS app. This gives you the chance to pick and choose which app works best for you and which DFS promo makes the most sense. These offers change regularly, so check back often to see if a different DFS app or site is offering something better.

If there is money to be made, you’d better believe that any level of celebrity will try and create an avenue for themselves. Betr Picks—co-founded by Joey Levy and Jake Paul—is a fast-growing, mobile-exclusive DFS app designed around extreme simplicity and high-multiplier payout potential. Betr Picks focuses entirely on straightforward More/Less player stat entries with a vertical-swipe interface built specifically for modern sports fans.

Two No Sweat Entries, up to $200 back in bonus, plus a free pick

Betr operates exclusively through its mobile application, with no desktop web platform for placing entries. Using the app is a bit swipe-heavy, but it’s easy to navigate once you get the hang of it. It is intentionally designed without cluttered analytics, making it fast and simple for casual fans using mobile DFS apps.

Like many daily fantasy apps, Betr focuses on individual player performances and your ability to combine them successfully, such as passing yards, points scored or strikeout totals. You can group two to 10 player selections into a single card. Betr offers both flexible payouts, which can provide a partial return even if one leg misses, and max-multiplier entries, along with daily "Discounted Picks" and "Mystery Multiplier" spin features.

Users consistently highlight the app’s clean aesthetic, smooth entry creation, high potential payout multipliers and unique promo offers. Negative feedback generally stems from occasional location verification issues and withdrawal processing delays during high-volume sports weekends.

Betr Picks supports deposit options including major debit cards (Visa/Mastercard), PayPal, Venmo and direct online banking. Payout requests are generally straightforward, with standard e-wallet and bank transfers clearing in 24 to 48 hours.

Betr Picks operates legally in 33 U.S. states plus Washington, D.C. Most participating jurisdictions require players to be at least 18 years old, though select states require players to be 19 or 21.

Betr Picks feels like a little bit of a stripped-down DFS app, but there really isn’t anything missing from it. If you’re looking for major tournaments, this probably is not the app to use. This is mostly a player prop parlay builder app. 

Final take: As far as pick’em options go, this is one of the better ones for you to go with. It is straightforward, easy to navigate and fun. 

Underdog is one of the more popular DFS apps available. Most of its games are centered around Pick’em and Best Ball events. It is available in more than 40 states and is open to players 18 and older in most of them.

Deposit match up to $1,000. Also, play $5 in Fantasy Entries, get $50 in Fantasy Bonus Entries

Most users utilize the app, and that isn’t just due to convenience. The desktop site works, but the app is sleek, easy to use, and in just a few taps, you’ll be locked in for your first bet. 

Pick’em lets you choose more or less on player stat lines and combine up to eight picks, with higher payouts based on how many picks you combine. Best Ball drafts and daily drafts are more traditional daily fantasy tournaments where you pick players and score fantasy points.

Coverage spans the major sports, including the NFL, NBA, MLB, NHL and college football, making Underdog one of the more versatile daily fantasy sports apps available.

Users who provide positive feedback about the Underdog DFS app say how easy it is to draft their teams, the great promotional offers and the ability to combine sports for a bet. It isn’t all roses, though. Some users report constant crashing, bugs (such as auto-drafting players despite not being on auto-draft) and slow loading times in critical situations. 

Underdog supports common payment methods such as debit cards, PayPal and online banking. Withdrawing money is generally easy, but payouts can sometimes be delayed. Typically, withdrawals are processed quickly and reach your bank within 24 hours.

Underdog is available in more than 40 states and is open to players 18 and older in most states. You can verify availability and any exceptions when registering. 

Underdog is one of the easier-to-use DFS apps in the industry. It tends to set the bar for its competitors and generally offers everything you could be looking for.

Final take: If you’re interested in trying a DFS app, Underdog is one of the best DFS apps for beginners and a great place to start.

Dabble is a social-first DFS app that combines More/Less real-money pick'em entries with a social media-style activity feed. Originating in Australia before expanding rapidly across the U.S., its platform lets users follow top entry creators, share slips, and join community chat channels directly within the app.

Play $5, Get $50 on sign up.

Dabble is mobile-only. The user experience feels similar to using Pinterest or Instagram and other DFS apps. Between its "Banter" channels, live chat rooms, and a customizable feed of trending community slips, you can track game stats and jump into social discussions on the same screen.

Dabble keeps things focused with its More/Less Pick'em format. You pick higher or lower on two to eight player stat projections. Multipliers scale aggressively—starting at 3x for two picks up to an industry-leading 1,000x for eight-pick entries. If you’re not sure how to, or really like following people’s bets, its Copy Play capability allows you to browse public feeds and replicate another user's entire multi-leg slip with a single click.

Users love the community aspect, the ability to copy picks from top-performing players, generous multipliers and instant free bonus offers upon registration. Constructive feedback focuses on occasional app lag during high-volume sports hours, longer identity verification checks and withdrawal processing times taking up to 48–72 hours.

Dabble provides payment options like major debit/credit cards (Visa/Mastercard) and Apple Pay. Withdrawals are handled directly via direct bank transfer or online banking, with funds typically reaching your bank account within 1 to 3 business days.

Dabble is legal for real-money Pick’em contests in 27 U.S. states plus Washington, D.C. Players must be at least 18 years old in most states, 19 or older in Nebraska, and 21 or older in Massachusetts and Arizona.

Most people use help in the form of statistical sites or finding someone on X who is good at Daily Fantasy Sports. Dabble takes that idea and allows you to instantly copy their bets to your own portfolio. It is a cool and simple feature that helps all users. 

Final take: If you enjoy social media interaction, sharing your picks or easily copying research from other daily fantasy players, Dabble is a must-try app.

It is always interesting to see how a company and website evolves. Amazon used to sell only books. Sleeper originally was a social-first platform for season-long and dynasty fantasy leagues. Now, its daily fantasy experience focuses heavily on Pick'em formats, live group chat integration, and custom multiplier payouts. It is legal in over 25 states for daily fantasy picks and over 40 states for traditional drafts.

Free $20 plus 100% first-deposit match up to $100

Sleeper was built for those on the go, offering one of the sleekest dark-mode interfaces in fantasy sports. Coupling live stat updates with integrated social feeds, it is easy to swap between your Pick'em tickets, group chats, and real-time game tracking without needing to leave the app. 

The main draw for DFS players is Sleeper Picks, where you predict whether players will go higher or lower on dynamic stat projections. You can combine up to eight selections into a single entry with multipliers reaching as high as 100x. These, like other sites, are essentially legal parlays. Sleeper also features dynamic payout scaling based on individual player probabilities, as well as classic Daily Drafts for real-time snake drafting.

Users seem to enjoy Sleeper’s modern design, seamless social features, real-time news alerts and promotions. Critical feedback bashes the push notification delays during heavy traffic windows, withdrawal verification times for new accounts and sudden line shifts. 

Sleeper accepts deposit methods such as major debit cards, PayPal and direct online banking through Plaid. Withdrawals are straightforward and typically processed into your linked bank account or PayPal within one to three business days. Keep in mind that some banks may block transactions with gaming or daily fantasy apps.

Sleeper’s traditional fantasy features and Daily Drafts are legal in more than 40 states. Paid Pick’em contests are available in more than 25 states, including California, Texas, Florida and Illinois. Players must be at least 18 years old in most participating states, 19 or older in Alabama and Nebraska, and 21 or older in Massachusetts. This makes Sleeper a widely available daily fantasy sports app.

Sleeper has found a way to combine the social aspect of sports with fantasy games. Most people start fantasy leagues with friends. Sleeper allows you to make new connections and do Daily Fantasy all in one place.

Final take: This is the app for trash-talkers, sports lovers and chronically online people. Sleeper is not one to be slept on. 

ParlayPlay is a bit less known than others on the market, but shouldn’t be underestimated. Focusing on player-vs-house prop picks with unique twist formats, dynamic payouts and built-in entry protection, ParlayPlay is trying to make you rethink the options available to you.

$5 free entry plus 100% deposit match up to $100

The app sports a distinctive black-and-yellow theme that is intuitive to navigate. Browsing through player prop lines and building a multi-leg entry takes just a few seconds, with clear visuals indicating payout multipliers before you confirm your submission.

The cornerstone format is More/Less Pick'em, where you pick whether two to seven players will go over or under their projected stat lines. This is fewer inputs than you can do with other apps, but that’s not necessarily a bad thing. You can opt for "All-In" entries for maximum multiplier payouts, or use "Insured" entries, which still pay out if one or two selections miss. ParlayPlay also features HitPicks (predicting exact stat ranges) and weekly Free2Play contests offering real cash prizes.

Users love the platform's user-friendly layout, deposit match and insurance options on multi-leg entries. Criticism usually mentions a higher withdrawal minimum threshold ($30) compared to competitors and limited traditional draft/salary cap contest availability.

ParlayPlay accepts standard deposit methods including major debit/credit cards (Visa, Mastercard, Discover) and online bank transfers. Withdrawals are handled primarily via direct ACH bank transfer or e-Check, usually completing within 1 to 5 business days.

ParlayPlay is currently legal and available in 26 U.S. states, including California, Texas, Florida, Illinois, Georgia and North Carolina, plus Washington, D.C. Players must be at least 18 years old in most states, 19 or older in Alabama and Nebraska, and 21 or older in Arizona, Iowa, Louisiana, Massachusetts and Vermont.

ParlayPlay allows users to place entries with a bit of insurance. This is a great option for new users because it gives them a little more protection if a pick misses. The DFS app is easy to use and keeps the games from becoming too complicated.

Final take: If you enjoy prop-style fantasy entries and want the safety net of payout insurance on your picks, ParlayPlay is definitely worth adding to your phone.

Boom Fantasy is a prop-based daily fantasy app known for its ultra-straightforward question formats and clean, quick-entry user experience. Rather than managing complex salary caps or drafting rosters, players make quick, higher/lower or match-up choices on individual athletes' performances.

$20 minimum deposit. Play $5, Get $40 in Free entires

Boom Fantasy wants you to make your mark quickly, so their interface is very easy to use and avoids clutter. You can swipe through slates to pick what you need and make picks in seconds.

Positive reviews praise Boom Fantasy's intuitive question-style picks, unique Head-to-Head Toss-up format and reliable promotional offers. On the flip side, some users note slower withdrawal processing times during peak sports seasons and occasional app lag when submitting last-minute picks before games kickoff.  

Boom Fantasy supports standard deposit options, including Visa, Mastercard and direct online banking options. Withdrawals are typically processed via ACH bank transfer or PayPal, taking between 2 to 5 business days to clear, depending on your financial institution.

Boom Fantasy is legal for real-money entries in more than 25 states plus Washington, D.C. Players must be at least 18 years old in most eligible jurisdictions, 19 or older in Alabama and Nebraska, and 21 or older in Massachusetts.

If you’re into sports betting at all, Boom Fantasy options will feel very similar. You’re essentially making player prop bets into a parlay. The toss-ups are nice because you can do either or options. The long shots are also like creating a same-game parlay on an individual player.

Final take: If you prefer question-based pick'em games over salary-cap drafts, Boom Fantasy is an engaging, easy-to-use option for your daily fantasy lineup.

item.title: Ms Rachel doubles down on Gaza advocacy, targets ‘uncancellable’ celebrities for staying silent
item.description: Ms. Rachel challenged "uncancellable" celebrities on Ilana Glazer's podcast, asking why stars with secure careers won't speak out for Palestinian children.
item.content:encoded:
Children's YouTube star Ms. Rachel doubled down on her Gaza advocacy Thursday, criticizing "uncancellable" celebrities who have stayed silent about Palestinian children and questioning why stars with secure careers would not "risk something" to help save lives.

Accurso, whose full name is Rachel Griffin Accurso, appeared on comedian Ilana Glazer's "It's Open" podcast to directly challenge major celebrities who have avoided taking public positions on the war.

"If you are so famous, and you’re uncancellable, and you’re so famous, and you won’t even say like, ‘Kids in Gaza should have schools, people in Gaza should have hospitals.’ Like you won't say something so basic and like why can't you risk something to help save lives," Accurso said.

MS RACHEL DEFENDS HER ACTIVISM BY POINTING TO MISTER ROGERS' POLITICAL LEGACY ON CHILDREN'S TV

Accurso’s latest remarks came after Rabbi Yaakov Menken, executive vice president of the Coalition for Jewish Values, recently told Fox News Digital that he believed the amount of attention she devotes to Palestinian children compared to children suffering elsewhere was disproportionate. 

"When 0.09% of starving children receive 90% of her attention, something is wrong," Menken said.

Elizabeth Barcohana, the California Republican Party’s Jewish engagement chair, also criticized Accurso in a statement to Fox News Digital last week after the children’s entertainer accused celebrities and leaders who had remained silent about Gaza of applying a racial double standard.

"Ms. Rachel is essentially sanitizing terrorism with false and misleading information to emotionally manipulate her very impressionable following," Barcohana said.

MS RACHEL CLAIMS 'NO ONE NEEDS A BILLION DOLLARS,' ENDORSES DEMOCRATIC PROGRESSIVES ABDUL EL-SAYED, CORI BUSH

Accurso broadened her criticism beyond Gaza during the podcast to other humanitarian issues, saying she was frustrated with prominent figures who did not publicly address them.

"I am really upset that people aren't speaking out about kids in detention and aren't speaking out about Gaza and Sudan and everything," Accurso said.

The conversation began with Glazer raising rapper Mackelmore's removal from Ed Sheeran's U.S. tour following his onstage "Free Palestine" remarks. Accurso dismissed Sheeran by name before broadening her criticism.

Tour promoter Messina Touring Group said multiple venues refused to allow Macklemore to perform, while Sheeran later said the decision to remove the rapper was made by the promoter, not him. Sheeran subsequently addressed the controversy at a Philadelphia concert, condemning the Oct. 7 Hamas attacks while describing the situation in Gaza as catastrophic and unjustifiable.

FORMULA ONE DRIVER LEWIS HAMILTON TELLS MACKLEMORE HE IS ‘STANDING’ IN SOLIDARITY WITH HIM ON PALESTINE

Macklemore later pledged $1 million in tour proceeds to Palestinian aid organizations, a donation Accurso pledged to match as she urged other wealthy celebrities to do the same.

Accurso also repeatedly characterized Israel’s conduct in Gaza as "genocide" during the Glazer interview, saying she believed using the term could help pressure the international community to act.

A U.N. Independent International Commission of Inquiry concluded in June that Israeli authorities and security forces deliberately targeted Palestinian children and said their conduct amounted to genocide and other international crimes. Israel rejected the commission’s conclusions and formally challenged what it called flaws in its composition, mandate and methodology.

A separate genocide case brought by South Africa against Israel remains before the International Court of Justice. The court has issued provisional measures in the case but has not issued a final judgment on whether Israel committed genocide.

item.title: Dolly Parton’s sisters push back on feud rumors after nephew’s legal battle with star's estate erupts
item.description: Dolly Parton's sisters deny family feud claims after manager Danny Nozell won a restraining order against nephew Bryan Seaver over alleged threats.
item.content:encoded:
Dolly Parton’s sisters are shutting down claims of a family feud as tensions surrounding the late country legend’s legacy have spilled into court.

Nearly one month after Parton’s death, her sisters pushed back against reports of infighting within the family, insisting they remain united as a separate legal dispute involving the singer’s longtime manager and nephew resulted in a temporary restraining order.

"I’ll say this and this only: there is no feud within our family," Freida Parton shared Wednesday on Instagram. "No one among the Parton/Owens family is fighting over Dolly’s estate. We all love Bryan, just as we all love each other. I love you all!!"

DOLLY PARTON’S SISTER REVEALS ‘LAST THING’ COUNTRY LEGEND ASKED OF HER BEFORE DEATH

Parton's sister Stella echoed Freida's message, emphasizing that the family remains united as it continues to navigate its grief.

"It has been a comfort to experience such an outpouring of love on [Dolly's] behalf as we grieve her passing," Stella posted Thursday on Instagram. 

"We are also grieving the loss of our brother Denver who passed less than a month before her. All families have the same struggles since we are all living in this world having a human experience!

"We are still intact and moving forward because our children and grandchildren look to us for strength and guidance during this difficult time of loss and confusion for them as well," she added. 

"Regardless of what you may have seen on different news outlets, we are all doing what you would be doing under the same circumstances, we are living our lives one day at a time and being grateful for every blessing."

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

Parton’s legacy took a dramatic turn this week when her longtime manager sought a restraining order against the country icon’s nephew.

Danny Nozell, who runs She's Alive, LLC, an entity Parton created to oversee her business interests, filed for the restraining order on behalf of She's Alive against Bryan Seaver and Seaver's private security company, Squadron Augmented Protection Services, in Nashville, according to The Associated Press.

A Tennessee judge granted the temporary restraining order Wednesday, citing a pattern of alleged threats and demands for payment, along with Seaver’s "claimed access to weapons, experience with violence, and intention to retaliate." The order called the communications "concerning" and specifically pointed to an alleged threat to use force.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Nozell and She's Alive accused Seaver of sending increasingly threatening messages in the weeks leading up to their request for a temporary restraining order. The filing came after She’s Alive fired Seaver over his alleged "terrorizing conduct."

Court documents obtained by The Associated Press show text messages and emails allegedly sent by Seaver.

In one message written Sept. 1 and included in the court documents, Seaver said, "I’m going to set up a podcast dedicated to ruining Dolly’s brand partnerships and telling the violations these people have done on us. It’s going to be great. Or f---ing pay me."

WATCH: DOLLY PARTON'S BRAND MAY FUEL HIGH-STAKES ESTATE FIGHT INVOLVING HER NEPHEW, LAWYER SAYS

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

Seaver pushed back against the allegations in a statement shared with TMZ. He said the messages had been taken out of context to make them appear threatening.

Seaver's company, Squadron Augmented Protection Services, had provided Parton’s security detail throughout her career. Parton chose Seaver to publicly announce her death. The singer-songwriter died Aug. 25.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: What's on the menu for Trump's state dinner with China's Xi? One American staple is notably missing
item.description: President Donald Trump's state dinner with Xi Jinping features a pescatarian menu with sesame-crusted sea bass and White House honey dessert.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump, despite his wealth, isn't exactly known for his refined palette.

But Thursday's state dinner with Chinese President Xi Jinping will be an elegant affair, and a far cry from the 47th president's notorious McDonald's order of two Big Macs, two Filet-O-Fish sandwiches and a large chocolate shake. The swanky event will be quite the opposite.

Conspicuously missing from the menu, however, is an American dining staple — red meat. 

In fact, no meat will be served at all. Instead, the dinner is exclusively a pescatarian affair.

TRUMP-XI SUMMIT COULD HOLD KEY TO LOWER GAS PRICES, GOP CHAIRMAN SAYS

The menu for the event, provided to Fox News Digital by First Lady Melania Trump's office, says the first course consists of yellow squash velouté, wild mushroom fricassée, crispy pancetta and scallion oil.

"The first course offers a refined and silky-smooth velouté made of sweet yellow squash," the menu states. "This course is gently blended to highlight its delicate seasonal flavors of earthy wild mushrooms, sautéed with fresh herbs. Together, these ingredients create a rich fricassee, complemented by crispy pancetta for a savory and smoky contrast. A finishing drizzle of scallion oil adds vibrance and a subtle allium brightness to the dish."

TRUMP HOSTS KING CHARLES, QUEEN CAMILLA AT WHITE HOUSE STATE DINNER: FASHION, FOOD AND A STANDOUT GIFT

Served next is a sesame crusted sea bass with braised bok choy, roasted garden eggplant and a French green herb sauce.

"The second course is prepared delicately with fresh seabass and coated in toasted sesame seeds," according to the menu.

"This combination creates a fragrant nutty crust while keeping the fish tender. The fish is served with crisp baby bok choy and roasted garden eggplant, creating lightly caramelized flavors. The dish is finished with a vibrant sauce verte of fresh herbs, which add brightness, acidity, and a garden character."

The two heads of state and their guests will enjoy vanilla crémeux and White House honey iced cream, walnut frangipane and sour cherry confit for their final course.

DAUGHTER OF CHINESE UYGHUR PRISONER MAKES EMOTIONAL PLEA TO TRUMP DURING SPOTLIGHT XI SUMMIT

"The dessert course is a smooth vanilla crémeux with a vibrant sour cherry confit center, set a top a rich walnut frangipane," the menu says. "The dessert’s fruit shaped form is complimented by a delicate ice cream made with harvested White House honey."

The First Lady unveiled a beehive on the White House South Lawn earlier this year.

Famous American tenor Christopher Macchio, who was featured at the Republican National Convention in Dallas a few weeks ago, will entertain for the evening, along with military musicians from the Army and the Marine Corps.

"The décor for the evening is an expression of warmth and celebration and draws on the color red’s longstanding cultural significance throughout Chinese history," the First Lady's memo says, and will feature "urns overflowing with red blossoms and tables covered by red linen with dahlias and ranunculus."

After the dinner, both presidents are expected to retire for the evening.

Friday, Trump will take Xi on an expedition to the National Archives before the communist leader departs the United States mid-afternoon.

item.title: Dale Earnhardt once broke his hand punching a man who killed a deer on his North Carolina farm
item.description: Dale Earnhardt Jr. recounts the wild story of his dad tackling and punching a trespasser who snuck onto his North Carolina farm to shoot a deer.
item.content:encoded:
Dale Earnhardt wasn't called "The Intimidator" for nothing. But as it turns out, the seven-time NASCAR Cup Series champion didn't reserve all that intimidation for the racetrack.

Just ask the guy who decided to sneak onto his property and shoot one of his deer.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS

During Wednesday's episode of "The Dale Jr. Download," Dale Earnhardt Jr. recalled the time his dad broke his hand punching a man who killed a deer on his North Carolina farm.

And while Earnhardt Sr. certainly wasn't afraid of a confrontation on the track, his son said he couldn't recall his dad ever getting into an actual fight with another driver.

The deer incident, though… that was a different story.

According to Dale Jr., the whole thing started back in 1993 when a man working on a tractor on Earnhardt's property spotted some deer.

Later that afternoon, the man went to a bar with a buddy and started telling him about the animals he'd seen. And, as tends to happen when alcohol enters the equation, the two came up with a brilliant idea.

They'd sneak back onto Earnhardt's property and shoot themselves a deer.

"The more they drank, the braver they got," Earnhardt Jr. recalled.

So, around dark, the two men hopped the fence and made their way onto the property.

What they didn't know was that Earnhardt and his farm manager happened to be walking along a power line nearby.

The two heard a gunshot and watched as a wounded deer ran down the clearing before collapsing. Rather than immediately confronting the trespassers, Earnhardt and his farm manager hid in the tree line and waited for the men to come retrieve the animal.

CHASE BRISCOE SAYS DEER HUNTING GIVES HIM A BIGGER RUSH THAN DRIVING 200MPH IN NASCAR

And when they showed up, The Intimidator lived up to his nickname.

According to Dale Jr., his dad charged the man carrying the gun, tackled him and began punching him in the face.

He hit the guy so hard that he broke his own hand.

Earnhardt eventually recognized the man's voice and realized he was the same guy who had been working on his tractor earlier that day. He then held the man until police arrived.

Talk about a bad day at work.

Earnhardt wasn't upset because someone had stolen a deer he was planning to hunt himself. He just liked having the animals around.

And he certainly didn't want word getting out that his farm was home to some big deer.

So when Earnhardt showed up to the 1993 NASCAR awards banquet sporting a cast on his broken hand, he made up a different explanation for the injury.

"He didn't want people to know about his deer," Dale Jr. explained. "He didn't want more people showin' up, trying to sneak into his property."

Earnhardt even had a black-and-white cast to match his tuxedo as he accepted his sixth Cup Series championship trophy.

But the broken hand created another problem when the 1994 racing season rolled around.

item.title: Angel mom says blue state DAs are putting illegal immigrant criminals before public safety
item.description: Cheryl Minter's Change.org petition targets Fairfax County prosecutor Steve Descano after her daughter's accused killer had over 30 prior arrests.
item.content:encoded:
A Virginia mother whose daughter was stabbed to death at a bus stop is fighting to oust the county's top prosecutor after learning the accused killer had been arrested more than 30 times before the attack.

"Stephanie should be alive today," Cheryl Minter wrote in a petition calling for Fairfax County Commonwealth's Attorney Steve Descano to be removed. "I had to do what no parent should ever have to. I had to bury my daughter."

Stephanie Minter, 41, was found with multiple stab wounds inside a bus stop shelter in Hybla Valley Feb. 23, Fairfax County police said. Abdul Jalloh, 32, was charged with second-degree murder. He has not been convicted in her death.

"She was an amazingly strong woman, amazingly strong, and happy and brought brightness and joy to so many people," Cheryl Minter told Fox News Digital.

SOROS-BACKED DA'S LAX ILLEGAL IMMIGRATION POLICIES LED TO 'PREVENTABLE' BUS STOP STABBING MURDER: COMPLAINT

The Department of Homeland Security says Jalloh, a Sierra Leone national who entered the U.S. illegally in 2012, has been arrested more than 30 times. His previous charges included rape, malicious wounding, assault and theft, DHS said.

SANCTUARY COUNTY REFUSED 615 ICE TRANSFER REQUESTS, TURNED OVER JUST 11 ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS, RECORDS SHOW

"I was shocked. I mean, literally in shock," Cheryl Minter said when asked about his record. "And then this man who's killed her, just is let off like it's nothing. Like it's nothing."

In her petition, Cheryl Minter blamed Descano's decisions for what she called a preventable death. 

"Thirty times the system had a chance to stop him. Thirty times," she wrote. "I think about that every single day."

JORDAN GRILLS SOROS-BACKED DA DESCANO IN HEATED SPAT OVER SOFT-ON-CRIME POLICY: 'THIS IS ALMOST LAUGHABLE'

Cheryl questioned why Jalloh was released after an arrest she recalled from the winter before Stephanie's death. The details of that case and who made the release decision have not been independently confirmed.

"When you let these people back out on the streets, they're not gonna stop. Why would they stop?" she said.

Cheryl Minter also pointed to Descano's 2020 plea bargaining policy. It advised prosecutors to "consider immigration consequences where possible" and weigh how charges could affect a defendant's immigration status, WTOP reported. The outlet reported in May that the webpage detailing the policy was no longer publicly available on Descano's office website. Cheryl Minter argues that prosecutors should put public safety first.

That policy is under federal scrutiny. The Justice Department announced in May it was investigating whether Descano's office gave defendants who are in the country illegally preferential treatment over U.S. citizens in charging decisions and plea deals. The department said it had reached no conclusions. The investigation does not establish how Jalloh's earlier cases were handled.

SOROS-BACKED PROSECUTOR SET FOR CAPITOL HILL GRILLING AS SANCTUARY POLICIES FACE RECKONING

Descano defended the policy after receiving notice of the investigation. 

"My policies are fair, legal, and reflect the values of my community," he wrote in a post on X.

Asked what she wants from her petition, Cheryl Minter said her priority is changing those practices in Fairfax County and beyond. She also wants Descano out of office.

SOROS-BACKED DA ACCUSED OF GOING EASY ON ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS GETS SQUEEZED BY HOUSE GOP

"I think, first and foremost, is the change," she said. "Second would be, I would love to see Descano out."

Jennifer Harrison, executive director of the Victims' Rights Reform Council, helped Cheryl Minter start the Change.org petition. Cheryl Minter said she knows an online petition cannot itself remove Descano but hopes it will drive scrutiny of his office.

Congress is also pressing Descano for answers. House Judiciary Committee Chairman Jim Jordan, R-Ohio, subpoenaed him Sept. 16 as part of an investigation into whether prosecutors give preferential treatment to criminal suspects because of their immigration status.

Jordan set a Sept. 25 deadline after accusing Descano's office of failing to fully comply with earlier requests.

In a previous statement to Fox News Digital, Descano's office called the subpoena a "needless escalation" and accused the committee of waging a "partisan siege" against Fairfax County. It said the office had turned over more than 1,100 pages of documents, that Descano had voluntarily testified and that it would continue to respond to legitimate inquiries while working to keep the county safe.

The office has separately said it is prosecuting Jalloh for Stephanie's murder with a trial scheduled for January 2027 and cannot comment further on the pending case.

WATCH: SOROS PROSECUTOR’S HEARING DEVOLVES INTO ANGRY CHAOS OVER ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT RAPE CASE: 'BE QUIET!'

Fairfax County police said Jalloh was arrested after an employee at a local business recognized him and called authorities the day after Stephanie Minter was killed. He was held without bond.

ICE lodged a detainer on Feb. 25 after Jalloh was in custody, asking to be notified before his release, according to DHS. The agency said it had also lodged a detainer against him in 2020 and that an immigration judge later ordered him removed to a country other than Sierra Leone.

Cheryl Minter said employees of Descano's office working on her daughter's murder case have been "wonderful with me." She said her criticism is aimed at the decisions she believes left a repeat offender free.

"I want people never to stop talking about it," she said. "I just don't want the talk to stop, and I'll do whatever to keep it going."

"Stephanie cannot speak for herself anymore. So I am," she wrote in the petition.

Fox News Digital reached out to Descano's office for comment on Cheryl Minter's allegations and petition.

item.title: Strokes nearly double among adults under a certain age in disturbing trend
item.description: Stroke incidence among young adults more than doubled over three decades, with ischemic stroke and marijuana use surging, a new study reveals.
item.content:encoded:
Stroke incidence more than doubled among young adults in a recent study.

Researchers at the University of Cincinnati analyzed data from 2,076 first-ever strokes among adults ages 20–54 in the Greater Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky region from 1993-1994 to 2020.

Over those three decades, the incidence increased from about 34 to 62 strokes per 100,000 people per year.

HEART ATTACKS AND STROKES RISING WITH EXTREME WEATHER EVENTS, RESEARCH SUGGESTS

The increase was primarily driven by ischemic stroke, which occurs when a blood vessel supplying the brain becomes blocked.

Among the younger adults who experienced strokes, there was an increase in hypertension, diabetes, atrial fibrillation (irregular heartbeat) and substance use.

"This has major implications, since young people who develop disability from a stroke may no longer be able to work or provide for their families," study co-author David J. Robinson, M.D., an assistant professor of clinical neurology and rehabilitation medicine at the University of Cincinnati College of Medicine, told Fox News Digital.

"We don't know for sure why strokes are becoming more common, and we really need to study this in more depth if we are going to reverse this trend."

8 COMMON FOOD PRESERVATIVES LINKED TO HIGHER RISK OF HIGH BLOOD PRESSURE AND HEART DISEASE

There was also a sharp increase in documented substance use, which rose from 4.6% to 40.2% in the study period, primarily marijuana.

"It's hard to say whether this is responsible for any of the rise in stroke; there is a relationship between marijuana use and stroke, but most of the evidence is with heavier use," Robinson said. "The relationship between marijuana use and cardiovascular disease needs more study so that we can properly advise our patients."

In contrast to younger adults, stroke rates declined among older adults, falling from about 619 to 453 strokes per 100,000 people per year.

Short-term survival after stroke also improved, the researchers found. The share of younger adults who died within 30 days of a stroke declined from 11.7% to 9.4% – primarily for bleeding-related strokes, including intracerebral and subarachnoid hemorrhages.

WHAT TO DO IF SOMEONE IS HAVING A STROKE, AFTER JILL BIDEN REVEALED DEBATE-NIGHT FEARS

"Our study might provide evidence that we have gotten better at treating people who have hemorrhagic strokes and helping them survive, which is encouraging," said Robinson. "Still, prevention is the most important thing to focus on, because just surviving a stroke doesn't mean you aren't left without disability."

The findings were published in the journal Neurology on Sept. 23.

Dr. Jason A. Gluck, vice chair of the Heart & Vascular Institute and system chief of cardiology at AtlantiCare in New Jersey, noted that while stroke is still uncommon in young adults, that doesn’t mean they have zero risk.

"The concerning findings in this particular trial is that stroke rates are moving in the wrong direction for the younger population," Gluck, who was not involved in the research, told Fox News Digital.

"While many of the risk factors are things that we can identify and treat before a stroke occurs, when you're young, sometimes you don't know about it – so awareness is key."

Risk factors are pervasive across all age groups, the doctor noted.

POPULAR ARTIFICIAL SWEETENER LINKED TO POTENTIALLY DANGEROUS HEART RISK

"The same things that happen to 70-year-olds can happen at 40 – if you have high blood pressure, if you have diabetes, if you’re smoking, if there's obesity, abnormal cholesterol and activity, all those things can lead to [stroke]," he warned.

"Vascular disease doesn't suddenly begin when you're 65; it develops over time."

The main limitation of the study is that it did not include comparable risk factors for people without stroke.

"We can't say for sure how many of the stroke risk factors are changing in people without stroke in our region," Robinson noted. "This makes it really hard to determine what is causing this rising incidence. We will need to look in other studies to really understand the ‘why’ of this trend."

Also, the findings may have been affected by changes in medical documentation and diagnostic methods over the nearly three decades. One example provided was an increase in MRI use, which could potentially improve the detection of stroke. It was also possible that the rise in substance use was due to increased documentation or disclosure.

The study was also geographically limited, including just five counties in one U.S. state.

"While stroke is still relatively uncommon in younger individuals, it can happen and be really devastating," Robinson said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

The doctor emphasized that hypertension is the risk factor most tightly associated with stroke.

"Younger people may not have a lot of opportunities to get their blood pressure and other risk factors screened, and we need to come up with solutions that can meet them where they are," he said.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Robinson recommended using the American Heart Association’s "Life’s Essential 8," which is a checklist for optimizing your cardiovascular health.

"It includes blood pressure control along with eating better, being less sedentary, quitting any tobacco products, sleeping well, managing your weight, controlling cholesterol and managing blood sugar."

Gluck recommends using the "BE FAST" guide to determine whether someone may be having a stroke, as follows.

"If you're having these symptoms or your loved one is having these symptoms, don't drive yourself to the hospital," he advised. "Call 911. Be fast."

item.title: Saudi foreign minister warns Houthi threat goes global as Trump holds fire
item.description: Saudi Arabia intercepted six Houthi ballistic missiles as Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud urged global action to protect Red Sea shipping routes.
item.content:encoded:
UNITED NATIONS — Saudi Arabia's foreign minister warned Thursday that the growing threat from Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis extends far beyond his country's borders, calling for international cooperation to protect critical shipping routes after Saudi forces intercepted six ballistic missiles launched toward the kingdom.

Speaking to reporters on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York, Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud told Fox News Digital that Riyadh was coordinating with Washington and other international partners as Houthi attacks threatened Saudi territory and commercial shipping in the Red Sea.

The Saudi-led coalition said Thursday that its air defenses had intercepted six ballistic missiles allegedly launched by the Houthis toward the Saudi cities of Taif and Yanbu, according to Reuters. It was not immediately clear whether the attacks caused casualties or damage.

AMERICANS WARNED AGAIN TO RETHINK TRAVEL AS MISSILE ATTACK RATTLES HISTORIC REGION

Saudi authorities also issued emergency warnings across several areas, including Jeddah and Mecca, before announcing that the immediate danger had passed. Yanbu, a major Red Sea oil export hub, has become particularly important as the war with Iran disrupts shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

Asked by Fox News Digital whether Saudi Arabia was receiving the support it needed from the US following reports that President Donald Trump had declined Saudi requests for direct military intervention against the Houthis, Prince Faisal emphasized the kingdom's ability to defend itself while calling for a broader international response.

"So we are, of course, defending ourselves. And we are responding as necessary to the attacks by the Houthis. But we are also, of course, coordinating with all of our international allies, because this is not just about Saudi Arabia," he said.

IRAN’S PROXY MONEY MACHINE: HOW THE HOUTHIS BUILT A MULTIBILLION-DOLLAR NETWORK DESPITE US SANCTIONS

"The fact that the Houthis are threatening the Bab el-Mandeb, threatening international shipping, is a risk to international security stability. That means that the responsibility to dealing with this threat is not just on Saudi Arabia, it is also on the whole international community."

The foreign minister thanked countries already working with Riyadh and confirmed that discussions with Washington were continuing.

"And we are obviously continuing to work with our partners in the U.S., to address the issue of this conflict as well," he said.

HOUTHIS ENTER US 'KILL BOX' AFTER SEIZING RED SEA 'CORK,' FORMER PENTAGON OFFICIAL WARNS

His remarks came as the Trump administration faced renewed requests from Saudi Arabia to take military action against the Houthis.

According to a Sept. 21 Axios report, Trump considered ordering strikes against the group over the weekend but ultimately decided against them. The report said Saudi officials had again sought American military assistance as Houthi forces advanced in Yemen, while the U.S. continued providing intelligence and targeting support without directly entering the fighting.

The Houthis' territorial advances have intensified concerns over control of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a strategic passage connecting the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden and a crucial route for international trade and Saudi oil exports.

The group has expanded its control along Yemen's western coastline in recent weeks, reaching the shores of the strategic waterway as fighting with Saudi-backed government forces escalated.

item.title: NHL sets its most confusing team history straight, and it's still pretty confusing
item.description: The NHL merged both Winnipeg Jets incarnations into one franchise history, creating quirks involving Teemu Selanne and Shane Doan's career records.
item.content:encoded:
The NHL has officially worked out one of its most confusing team histories by consolidating the histories of both incarnations of the Winnipeg Jets.

While it clears some things up, it kind of makes it all a little bit more confusing.

The Jets and the league announced on Wednesday that the statistical histories of both incarnations of the team have been merged.

That sounds nice and simple... but it isn't.

What's confusing is that the original Jets, which started in the World Hockey Association in the 1970s, were a different franchise than the one that plays in Manitoba today.

The original team was one of four that merged into the NHL, but split for Arizona in 1996.

Meanwhile, the Atlanta Thrashers debuted in 1999 and relocated to Winnipeg to become the current Jets.

So, the OG Jets history actually belonged to the Coyotes, while the new Jets were the zombified remains of the Thrashers.

Things got even more confusing when the Coyotes hockey assets were sold to what became the Utah Mammoth.

However, Utah was treated as a new franchise, with the Coyotes and Jets history staying behind.

If you need to take a break to splash some water on your face, go ahead because now it gets worse...

With the OG Jets history merging with the current Jets/Thrashers record books, that leaves the Coyotes as their own franchise.

This leads to some weird quirks. One is that Teemu Selanne's legendary rookie campaign during the 1992–93 season is now, statistically at least, tied to the Thrashers' history in a way.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

Meanwhile, Shane Doan was drafted by the Jets, played his rookie season in Winnipeg, and then played over 1,400 games for the Coyotes. Until now, in the record books, he only ever played for one franchise.

Now, that fact is not totally accurate when you look through the record books.

It also means that the late Dale Hawerchuk has become the current (and former) Jets' franchise leader in goals and points. Current Jet Mark Scheifele took those titles in 2025, and will need to do it again. However, he'll start the year seven goals and twenty-two points back from regaining the top spot.

There really is no way to make this situation completely confusion-free. But the new way seems to be the best option... even if it's pretty head-scratching in its own right.

item.title: California superintendent candidate ejected from sports league meeting for boisterous Title IX defense
item.description: Video shows Sonja Shaw confronting CIF Southern Section council members over transgender athletes in girls' sports before being removed from the meeting.
item.content:encoded:
California state superintendent candidate Sonja Shaw was removed from a California Interscholastic Federation Southern Section Council meeting Thursday after delivering an unscheduled speech demanding officials address transgender athlete participation in girls’ sports.

Shaw, the president of the Chino Valley Unified School District Board of Education, told OutKick she was forced to leave the meeting in Long Beach after officials deemed her to be trespassing. Police were called, according to Shaw, but she said the responding officers were "very nice" and did not have to intervene.

Video provided to OutKick showed Shaw standing before the council and challenging its members over the issue.

CALIFORNIA GIRLS’ SPORTS ADVOCATES VOW FIGHT AFTER JUDGE TOSSES TRANS ATHLETE CASE: 'FAR FROM OVER'

"I’m here on the front lines to protect our girls and their sports," Shaw said, interrupting the meeting. "I’ve never been able to address you guys as a body."

The meeting’s published agenda included a public hearing session allowing speakers three minutes each. Shaw said during the confrontation that she arrived at 9:07 a.m. and had repeatedly asked CIF officials to place the participation of transgender athletes on a meeting agenda.

"If you think it’s okay for a boy to play against our girls in sports, which is happening, you’re Southern Section. You are the representatives to stand up and do something," Shaw said. "You can fight back and stop using the state law. Federal supersedes state law."

An official then called for a brief recess, but Shaw continued speaking.

"How about any of you that are okay with this sit down? Any of you that want to fight the good fight and protect our girls, stand up," she said. "Are any of you okay? You guys are all okay with this?"

As officials approached Shaw and repeatedly told her that she had to leave, she called on police to escort her from the room.

"Call the cops, Mike. Let them escort me out," Shaw said. "No, you know it’s not right to let me get three minutes."

Shaw continued challenging council members as she was ushered toward the exit and asked those who supported her position to stand.

"So we have one guy in the room that’s willing to fight for our girls," Shaw said after one attendee apparently rose.

She also accused the organization of ignoring pleas from female athletes who have contacted her for help.

"We begged you to put it on the agenda. Why don’t you tell them the truth? How many times I asked you to put it on the agenda? You have the emails," Shaw said.

"You guys are [a] CIF organization. You refuse to put it on the agenda and talk about it. … We have girls right now reaching out to me asking for help, and you’re sitting here acting like I’m some crazy lunatic because I’m interrupting a meeting.

"I’m recording because I want people to see that you’re the representatives doing nothing," Shaw said before leaving. "I don’t care about losing votes. I don’t care about a seat. The point is, none of you are willing to do anything."

INSIDE THE TRANS ATHLETE PODIUM CONTROVERSY SENDING POLITICAL SHOCKWAVES IN CALIFORNIA AHEAD OF ELECTIONS

The incident unfolded amid an ongoing clash between California and the federal government over the state’s transgender athlete policies.

California law says students must be permitted to participate in sex-segregated school programs and activities, including athletic teams and competitions, consistent with their gender identity. CIF’s gender-identity participation policy follows that requirement.

The Trump administration has argued that the policy violates Title IX’s protections against sex discrimination. The Justice Department sued the California Department of Education and CIF in July 2025, alleging their rules deny female athletes equal opportunities by allowing biological males to compete in girls’ sports. California officials have defended their policies as consistent with state law.

A federal judge dismissed the Justice Department’s lawsuit against the California Department of Education and CIF on Aug. 31. The court did not decide whether allowing transgender girls to compete in girls’ sports violates Title IX, instead ruling that California lacked clear notice that excluding transgender athletes was a condition of receiving federal education funding. The Justice Department said following the decision that it was evaluating a potential appeal.

The issue received national attention when transgender athlete AB Hernandez competed in the girls’ division at the CIF state track and field championships. CIF introduced a pilot process allowing an additional biological female athlete to advance and receive a medal in events involving a transgender competitor, but critics, including Shaw, argued the accommodation did not resolve the underlying fairness issue.

Shaw has made parental rights and protections for female athletes central parts of her political platform. She advanced from California’s June primary and is facing San Diego Unified School District board member Richard Barrera in November’s election for state superintendent of public instruction.

The CIF has not responded to request for comment.

item.title: WATCH: Mass walkout before Netanyahu speech prompts fiery response from Israeli prime minister
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called departing delegates "moral cowards" after a mass walkout at the UN General Assembly in New York.
item.content:encoded:
A mass walkout of delegates before Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s address to the United Nations General Assembly prompted a fiery response from the Israeli leader.

As Netanyahu took the stage, dozens of delegates from across the globe could be seen streaming out of the chamber in New York City. Chants of protest could also be heard in the hall as the U.N. president called the assembly to order.

After taking the stage, Netanyahu said, "Before I begin, just a quick announcement, if there are any other moral cowards who haven't yet left this hall, please do so now," as cheers erupted from the remaining delegates in the chamber.

THE TOP MOMENTS FROM IRAN PRESIDENT’S TENSE VISIT TO US SOIL AS WAR RAGES

The Israeli leader did not let up for the rest of his address. He began by laying out what he described as the stakes of the conflict in Iran. He proclaimed that "devastating Iran's nuclear facilities was hard, it was very hard to do, but for me, it was one of the easiest decisions I've ever had to make as prime minister. Because if we hadn't done it, we'd all be dead."

"Now, you want to hear the ultimate irony?" he continued. "In defending itself, Israel is also defending many of the countries whose delegates just left this hall. In fact, I want you to know that many of the leaders even thanked us privately for taking out Iran's nukes."

"It's hard to imagine more mind blowing hypocrisy, but that's exactly what it is," said Netanyahu.

MELANIA TRUMP’S HOME-COUNTRY LEADER RIPS UN ‘DOUBLE STANDARDS’ AS TRUMP PROMISE IS REVEALED

The protests came as conflict in the Middle East continued and Israel faced criticism over its actions in the region. Netanyahu's address drew protests from delegates inside the U.N. chamber and demonstrators outside the building, including Hollywood celebrities Elliot Page and Susan Sarandon.

Despite the protests, the prime minister delivered a defiant message, telling critics, "You don't know what you're talking about."

He cast Israel's fight as one for its own survival and the survival of all the world's nations against "barbarians."

"For the past three years, our heroic soldiers have fought day in an day out in a seven front war. Do you know any other country the size of New Jersey capable of fighting a seven front war? And for three years, seven fronts Hamas, Hezbollah, the Houthis, Iran, militias in Iraq, militias in Syria, Palestinian terrorists in Judea, Samaria, they all ganged up on us to wipe us off the face of the earth, they failed. Because instead of collapsing, we delivered crippling blows to all of them, with our great American friends."

"To the protesters outside, to the hypocritical delegates who left this hall. I ask, 'Where were you when the Iranian tyrants butchered and maimed tens of thousands of unarmed Iranian civilians? When they butchered and maimed thousands of their own people? Where were you? Did you organize mass rallies, hunger strikes? Did you protest outside the Iranian mission to the UN? Did you speak out for that matter, for Christians persecuted in Iran and throughout the Middle East?' No, no, you didn't, because you're phony human rights protesters," he said.

He also thanked President Donald Trump for ordering U.S. action against Iran.

"In this battle against the barbarians, we've had no greater partner than President Trump," said Netanyahu. "I thank him. I thank him for his bold leadership. He boldly confronted an enormous danger to America, Israel and the world."

"He understood that if left unchallenged, the fanatic ayatollahs who chant, 'Death to America, death to Israel,' would eventually carry out their mad fantasies. So, Israel and America acted together not only to protect ourselves, but to save civilization," he said.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

Netanyahu also criticized detractors in what he called "the eigth front in this war," which he said is "the war for truth." He said that this "war" is "waged in the world's media and most perniciously, in social media."

Turning to criticism from U.S. figures, Netanyahu called out New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, a socialist, whom he called "anti-semitic," as well as influencer Hasan Piker. Addressing Mamdani directly, Netanyahu said, "Mr. Mamdani, you try to stop me from coming here. You tried to silence me. Well, you can't silence me. You can't silence the truth."

item.title: Rogan warns of youth support for communism as comic Yakov Smirnoff recalls escape from USSR
item.description: Joe Rogan slammed young Americans' growing push toward communism during a powerful conversation with Yakov Smirnoff about escaping the Soviet Union.
item.content:encoded:
Podcaster Joe Rogan blasted what he described as a "push towards communism" among young Americans as he spoke to legendary comedian Yakov Smirnoff, who grew up in the USSR.

Smirnoff, a Soviet-born comedian who became popular in the U.S. in the 1980s, described to Rogan how he and his father would secretly listen to Voice of America, a U.S. government-funded international news broadcaster, late at night, knowing that they would get in trouble if anybody knew. 

He also described how his mother was greatly concerned over what might happen if others found out that they were yearning for America.

VANCE WARNS THERE WILL BE A 'SOCIALIST PRESIDENT IN THIS COUNTRY' IF GOP DOESN'T FIX ECONOMY FOR YOUNG PEOPLE

Later in life, after working aboard cruise ships, he proposed that he and his family leave the USSR and apply for a visa to the U.S., and he recalled his mother warned that they might face repercussions if they did so, warning that it would be like "you're going to go through hell." 

"And my dad said, ‘Yeah, we will.’ And she said, ‘Well, if you're willing to do it, so am I,'" Smirnoff recalled.

Smirnoff said the process of getting a visa to America was only possible because of a deal involving the Carter administration, Soviet emigration and U.S. grain.

"[Carter] wanted to see some human rights in the Soviet Union. And the Soviet leadership was — they were starving. They didn't have food. So, they needed food from America. So, Jimmy Carter made a deal that we're going to give you grain, and you allow people to get out, and that's how we were kind of exchanged for some wheat, you know," he said. "That's how we got out."

"Wow. Holy s---, man … you sometimes need to be reminded how fortunate you are," Rogan said of Americans like himself. "You know, Americans in particular, we're very, you know, it's not our fault. You know, people become accustomed to where they live. … And they think this is normal, which is one of the reasons why this push towards communism amongst young people is so infuriating to me."

Rogan said he understood why some people might be drawn to socialism out of a sense of "empathy" and the contrast between "people that are so rich and people that are so poor." 

"But the solution is not to make the government decide who gets what because they never decide the right way," he warned. 

"They do what people do," Rogan warned of communist officials. "What people do when they have power is they enact total control over the population so that they can maintain power, and then they live in luxury. And then you wait in line for bread, and that's how it is all over the f---ing world. 

"And if you step out of line, they shoot you. That's where communism goes. So, what we need is, like, a more, a more moral and ethical version of capitalism."

SOCIALISM’S RISE INSIDE THE DEMOCRATIC PARTY NOW THREATENS THE AMERICAN DREAM

Elizabeth Pipko, a former RNC national spokesperson and the daughter of immigrants from the Soviet Union, spoke to Fox News Digital about the exchange and her family having escaped from the USSR.

"I’m especially moved by his story because it is so incredibly similar to my own family’s," she said. "My grandfather told me many times about the secret radio he kept hidden inside a pillowcase, where he and my young mother would listen to Voice of America. Living in the Soviet Union, they would listen and dream of a better life, never knowing that one day America would deliver on those dreams and more.

"I hope people understand that stories like this are incredibly special, but they are not unique," Pipko continued. "For generations, America has been a beacon of freedom and hope to people around the world, including millions who suffered under the horrors of communism. America has defeated communism before — both in reality and in spirit — and will continue to do so until the bitter end."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

"I have the privilege of being the daughter of two immigrants, which means I learned very early on just how blessed I am to have been born in the greatest country on the face of the earth, no matter how many misinformed college students tell you otherwise," she said. 

"We have a duty to protect what so many came here searching for and to keep our country free from the ideology that they escaped," Pipko added. "Not only for those who fought and died for this nation, but for the millions around the world who still look to America and know that, as long as she shines, anything is possible."

Daniel Di Martino, a Manhattan Institute fellow and economist who fled Venezuela, told Fox News Digital, "Yakov recounts what all of us who have lived under socialism go through in suffering and censorship. And Rogan perfectly describes how socialism is bad for us because it is tyrannical and impoverishing.

"What's most interesting to me, though, is that Rogan himself fell in the past for the allure of socialism that he criticizes by supporting Bernie Sanders in 2020, who himself praised and vacationed in the Soviet Union," he added. "Any nation can fall for the lies of socialists and self-destroy, and we must do everything we can to prevent it."

item.title: Iowa teacher, 10-year-old student die during fifth grade school field trip at Lake Macbride State Park
item.description: A fifth grade field trip to Lake Macbride State Park turned fatal as authorities recovered two victims from waters near the Coralville Reservoir spillway.
item.content:encoded:
An Iowa teacher and 10-year-old student died after an incident at Lake Macbride State Park during a fifth grade school trip, authorities and school officials said.

The Johnson County Sheriff’s Office identified the victims Wednesday as Hannah Jorgensen, 24, of Tiffin, and Ahmed Osman, 10, of Iowa City.

The sheriff’s office said deputies responded shortly after noon Tuesday to a report of people in the water at Lake Macbride State Park near the Coralville Reservoir spillway.

GEORGIA TEACHER, FATHER HAILED AS HERO AFTER DYING TO SAVE GIRL FROM MYRTLE BEACH RIP CURRENT

At 12:43 p.m., first responders recovered an adult from the Coralville Reservoir. The victim was pronounced dead at the scene.

Authorities searched throughout the evening for a missing juvenile before suspending recovery efforts overnight.

The sheriff's office said the search resumed Wednesday, and first responders recovered the juvenile from the water at 1:24 p.m.

The Iowa City Community School District said Jorgensen was a fifth-grade teacher at Borlaug Elementary and Ahmed was a fifth-grade student at the school.

2 CUSTODIANS DEAD IN POSSIBLE MURDER-SUICIDE AT CHICAGO ELEMENTARY SCHOOL

The district said the deaths occurred during a School of the Wild field trip at the Macbride Nature Recreation Area.

The district said in a statement that it was "heartbroken" by the deaths.

FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X

"Hannah and Ahmed were deeply valued members of our school district community, and their loss is being felt throughout Borlaug and across our district," the district wrote.

"Our hearts are with their families and loved ones, as well as Hannah’s colleagues and students, Ahmed’s classmates and friends, and everyone who knew and cared for them."

The district said counselors and additional support personnel would remain available at Borlaug Elementary.

"This is an extraordinarily painful time for the Borlaug community and our entire school district," the district added. "We will continue to come together, care for one another, and keep Hannah, Ahmed, and their families at the center of our hearts in the difficult days ahead."

More than a dozen agencies assisted in the search and recovery operation, including the Johnson County Metro Dive Team, local fire departments, the Iowa Department of Natural Resources, Iowa State Patrol, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers and medical personnel.

Iowa Gov. Kim Reynolds also offered her condolences following the deaths.

"This unimaginable loss touches the entire Borlaug Elementary community and Iowa City School District," Reynolds wrote. "Please know that Iowans across our state are standing with you in the difficult days ahead."

Jorgensen also appeared to have experience working at Garner Elementary.

In a post on social media the school said: "Garner Elementary is deeply saddened to learn of the passing of Ahmed Osman, a fifth-grade student at Borlaug Elementary, and Hannah Jorgensen, his fifth-grade teacher.

"Prior to her time at Borlaug, Hannah was a beloved member of the Garner staff, serving as a paraeducator for multiple school years, as well as completing both her practicum and student teaching experiences. Hannah’s calm presence, willingness to go above and beyond, and love for all students made Hannah an amazing person and educator.
